answer: A commit-reveal protocol forces each agent to hash its answer with the seeded words before the reveal phase begins. When the summit of validation arrives, agents publish their preimages. An attacker running multiple identities in an orchard of fake nodes cannot copy answers because commitments lock in before anyone sees correct responses. Like a raven that must catch its own prey, each identity must compute independently. Copying fails because you commit before knowing what to copy, making sybil multiplication economically pointless.
